nodes.label: dependency-track-api-server StatefulSet sizing
nodes.rationale: Dependency-Track enforces a hard minimum 4GB JVM heap at startup; heap is ~80% of the memory limit (MaxRAMPercentage), so the limit must be >=5Gi. 6Gi is used for headroom (~4.8GB heap). Lowering below 5Gi crashes the API server. Hard node affinity pins it to zone fr01 next to its ceph-rbd-fr01 PV.

nodes.label: dependency-track-frontend Deployment
nodes.rationale: 3 replicas spread by podAntiAffinity across hostnames, with soft zone-fr01 preference; tiny resource envelope (10m CPU / 64Mi limit) because it only serves static assets and proxies to the API server.

nodes.label: Dependency-Track Azure AD OIDC integration
nodes.rationale: ALPINE_OIDC_* on the API server plus OIDC_* on the frontend both read issuer/client-id from the dependency-track-env Secret; user provisioning and team synchronization are on, mapping the email claim to usernames and the groups claim to DT teams.

nodes.label: CNPG PgBouncer pooler (feather-core-cluster-pg-pooler-rw)
nodes.rationale: Default shared Postgres entrypoint for apps in the cluster: connection pooling in front of the CNPG primary keeps idle app pools from exhausting max_connections. Apps that send unsupported libpq startup parameters must bypass it.

nodes.label: PriorityClass feather-standard
nodes.rationale: Injected via HelmRelease postRenderers kustomize patches because the upstream charts expose no priorityClassName value; mid-tier eviction priority for non-critical business apps.

nodes.label: logs.onelitefeather.net/env=prod pod label
nodes.rationale: Cross-cutting log-routing label applied on every app's pod template so Alloy can select and tag production logs; a sibling logs.onelitefeather.net/format=json marks workloads emitting structured JSON.

nodes.label: StorageClass ceph-rbd-fr01
nodes.rationale: Zone-fr01 Ceph RBD block storage; workloads using it must pin node affinity to zone fr01 since RBD volumes are ReadWriteOnce and zone-local.

nodes.label: HelmRelease grafana
nodes.rationale: Stateless 2-replica Deployment (persistence disabled, useStatefulSet false) with all state in the shared CNPG Postgres, so pods are disposable; topology spread with whenUnsatisfiable DoNotSchedule forces the two replicas onto different hosts, and a PDB minAvailable 1 protects drains.

nodes.label: Grafana Loki datasource (uid loki)
nodes.rationale: derivedFields extracts trace_id from JSON log lines and links to the Tempo datasource, which is why structured-JSON workloads carry logs.onelitefeather.net/format=json.

nodes.label: Grafana Tempo datasource (uid tempo)
nodes.rationale: tracesToLogsV2 points back at Loki and tracesToMetrics/serviceMap at Mimir, closing the traces<->logs<->metrics correlation loop across the three backends.

nodes.label: Grafana unified alerting HA (gossip over grafana-headless:9094)
nodes.rationale: Two Grafana replicas would each fire the same alert; ha_peers via the headless Service plus POD_IP-derived listen/advertise addresses form an Alertmanager cluster so notifications are deduplicated. Legacy alerting is explicitly disabled.

nodes.label: Discord contact point (uid discord_webhook)
nodes.rationale: Provisioned as a `secret:` block with a placeholder URL that Flux's valuesFrom overwrites at targetPath alerting.contactpoints\.yaml.secret.contactPoints[0]..., keeping the real webhook out of git.

nodes.label: discord.title / discord.message notification templates
nodes.rationale: Go template delimiters are double-escaped with backtick literals so Helm does not consume them at render time; the message surfaces alertname, summary, severity and the Flux customresource kind/namespace/name.

nodes.label: Default notification policy (route all to discord)
nodes.rationale: Single flat route grouped by alertname with group_wait 30s / group_interval 5m / repeat_interval 4h — deliberately no per-severity subtrees, since every provisioned rule already carries a severity label in its message body.

nodes.label: Alert flux-core-layer-not-ready
nodes.rationale: Instant query on gotk_resource_info{customresource_kind="Kustomization", ready="False"}, threshold >0 for 5m; noDataState OK so a scrape gap does not page, execErrState Alerting so a broken query does.

nodes.label: Alert core-infra-helmrelease-not-ready
nodes.rationale: Deliberately name-filtered to a hand-maintained allowlist (envoy, cert-manager, rook-ceph, cnpg, mariadb-operator, mimir, loki, tempo, grafana, cloudflare-tunnel-ingress-controller, metallb, dragonfly) so only foundation HelmReleases page, not every app.

nodes.label: Alert cnpg-backup-stale
nodes.rationale: cnpg_collector_last_available_backup_timestamp never updates for plugin-based (barman-cloud) backups — confirmed stuck at 0 even after real completed backups — so the rule reads cnpg_backup_stopped_at_seconds from kube-state-metrics customResourceState on the Backup CR instead, alerting past 24h.

nodes.label: Alert cnpg-backup-failing
nodes.rationale: Same dead-metric problem as cnpg-backup-stale: cnpg_collector_last_failed_backup_timestamp never fires for plugin backups, and failed Backup CRs never get a stoppedAt, so the rule counts Backup CRs with phase=failed whose createdAt falls in the last 24h, OR vector(0) to avoid no-data.

nodes.label: Alert mariadb-galera-backup-job-failed
nodes.rationale: Uses generic kube_job_status_failed in the mariadb-galera namespace rather than an operator metric, so it works regardless of how the backup CronJob is implemented.

nodes.label: Grafana file dashboardProviders (7 folders)
nodes.rationale: Dashboards are inlined into the HelmRelease values (~27k lines) and provisioned from disk under /var/lib/grafana/dashboards/<folder> across Kubernetes, Controllers, Observability, Databases, Applications, Storage and Minecraft folders; editable:true means UI edits are allowed but non-persistent.

nodes.label: Ceph cluster / OSD / pools dashboards (Storage folder)
HTTPRoute harbor (harbor.apps.onelite.feather)
nodes.rationale: Internal front door for UI/manual access only: Envoy terminates TLS with a step-issuer cert (internal-certs layer) and forwards plain HTTP to the harbor nginx Service. Image pulls deliberately go through the public Cloudflare tunnel host instead, so externalURL stays harbor.onelitefeather.dev.

nodes.label: Envoy Gateway 'eg' https listener (namespace envoy)
nodes.rationale: Single shared Gateway that every internal *.apps.onelite.feather HTTPRoute attaches to via parentRefs sectionName https; TLS terminates here so backend Services stay plain HTTP.

nodes.label: Ingress harbor-cloudflare-tunnel (harbor.onelitefeather.dev)
nodes.rationale: External registry endpoint for push+pull matching externalURL. Cloudflare caps request bodies at 100MB, so pushes MUST use a chunked client — regctl chunks by default (BlobMax 4MB / BlobChunk 512KB) and is fine while blobChunk stays <100MB, whereas a plain `docker push` of a single >100MB layer fails through the tunnel.

nodes.label: cloudflare-tunnel IngressClass (external front door)
nodes.rationale: Public exposure without an inbound LoadBalancer: the strrl cloudflare-tunnel-ingress-controller programs Cloudflare tunnel routes from Ingress objects, with backend-protocol:http because TLS is terminated at Cloudflare's edge.

nodes.label: Secret harbor-secret (harbor.env)
nodes.rationale: One Secret multiplexed across every Harbor credential surface: admin password, external Postgres password, external Redis/Dragonfly password and the S3/RGW access keys all read from it via existingSecret.

nodes.label: PodDisruptionBudget harbor-registry (minAvailable 1)
nodes.rationale: The registry runs a single replica because chunked uploads are session-bound to one pod; minAvailable:1 (not maxUnavailable) keeps that pod up across voluntary disruptions so node drains/updates cannot silently kill the registry mid-push — draining its node requires a deliberate cordon/force.

nodes.label: PodDisruptionBudget harbor-nginx (maxUnavailable 1)
nodes.rationale: nginx is the single front service all Harbor traffic funnels through, so at least one pod must survive node drains to avoid 504s.

nodes.label: HelmRelease harbor (chart =1.19.1)
nodes.rationale: expose.type clusterIP with chart TLS disabled: the release intentionally owns no Ingress of its own, leaving both front doors (Envoy HTTPRoute internal, Cloudflare tunnel Ingress external) as standalone objects pointing at the single `harbor` Service.

nodes.label: Harbor nginx front proxy (Service harbor:80)
nodes.rationale: Single-endpoint exposure: one ClusterIP Service fronts nginx which does all path routing (portal vs core vs /v2), so external and internal front doors need no path knowledge; nginx serves plain HTTP on :80 since TLS terminates at Envoy or Cloudflare.

nodes.label: Harbor registry + registryctl (single replica, JSON logs)
nodes.rationale: replicas:1 with upload_purging enabled (168h age, 24h interval); REGISTRY_LOG_FORMATTER=json pairs with the logs.onelitefeather.net/format=json pod label so Loki can parse trace ids.

nodes.label: Harbor Trivy vulnerability scanner
nodes.rationale: Hard-pinned to zone fr01 (requiredDuringScheduling) because it needs its own RWO PVC for the vulnerability DB; scans os+library across all severities with securityCheck vuln.

nodes.label: Harbor imageChartStorage on Ceph RGW S3 (rook-ceph-rgw-feather-s3)
nodes.rationale: Registry blobs live in the in-cluster Rook RGW bucket over plain HTTP (secure:false, v4auth) with disableredirect:true so clients never receive a redirect to an internal RGW endpoint they cannot reach.

nodes.label: Harbor OTLP trace export to alloy-receiver
nodes.rationale: trace.provider otel at sample_rate 1 pointing at alloy-receiver.grafana.svc:4318 /v1/traces, insecure in-cluster; this is the hop that makes Harbor traces reachable from the Tempo datasource.

nodes.label: PriorityClass feather-high
nodes.rationale: Reserved for platform services other workloads depend on (registry, observability UI) so they win scheduling and survive eviction pressure.

nodes.label: Monitoring split-out (loki/mimir/tempo in a wait:false Kustomization)
nodes.rationale: Loki, Mimir and Tempo are excluded from base-apps and managed by the dedicated wait:false monitoring Kustomization so their external Ceph-RGW S3 backend cannot block the base-apps -> apps dependency chain when RGW is degraded.

nodes.label: Secret cf-origin-tls (kubernetes.io/tls from SOPS crt+key)
nodes.rationale: Cloudflare origin certificate assembled from two separately SOPS-encrypted files (cf-origin-tls.sops.crt / .sops.key) via secretGenerator files: mapping into tls.crt/tls.key.

nodes.label: HelmRelease leantime
nodes.rationale: Single replica with readOnlyRootFilesystem:false (Leantime writes into its webroot) and both chart ingress and chart httpRoute disabled — exposure is exclusively the standalone Cloudflare tunnel Ingress.

nodes.label: Secret n8n-secrets (N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY et al.)
nodes.rationale: Must carry all four keys the chart reads (N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY / N8N_HOST / N8N_PORT / N8N_PROTOCOL); losing N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY makes every stored credential permanently undecryptable, so the value must stay stable forever.

nodes.label: HelmRelease n8n
nodes.rationale: N8N_PROXY_HOPS=1 because exactly one reverse proxy (Envoy) sits in front; webhook.url drives WEBHOOK_URL and N8N_EDITOR_BASE_URL so generated links use the public-facing host even though the chart Ingress is off.

nodes.label: n8n queue mode (1 main + 2 BullMQ workers)
nodes.rationale: Executions are offloaded to worker pods via a Bull queue in Dragonfly; multiMain stays off because multi-main HA requires an enterprise license, so the single main pod remains the only UI/API instance.

nodes.label: CNPG primary rw service (feather-core-cluster-pg-rw) — pooler bypass
nodes.rationale: n8n connects to the CNPG primary directly instead of the shared PgBouncer pooler because it sends statement_timeout as a libpq startup parameter, which PgBouncer rejects ("unsupported startup parameter: statement_timeout") unless added to ignore_startup_parameters — and changing that on the shared pooler would affect every other app.

nodes.label: Shared Dragonfly instance (dragonfly.dragonfly.svc:6379)
nodes.rationale: One operator-managed Dragonfly replaces all per-app Redis deployments, partitioned by numbered logical DB (n8n Bull queue on 11; Harbor core 0 / jobservice 1 / registry 2 / trivy 5 / harbor 6 / cache layer 7). No Sentinel is needed because the operator exposes a stable master endpoint. See docs/dragonfly-redis-cutover.md.

nodes.label: node-red base-apps Kustomize overlay
nodes.rationale: secretGenerator is an empty list with the old minio-password-secret entry commented out — a deliberate placeholder kept for the disabled MinIO integration.

nodes.label: HelmRelease node-red
nodes.rationale: persistence.size is pinned to 10Gi to match the existing PVC capacity: the chart default is smaller and a PVC cannot shrink, which made every helm upgrade fail. Chart version is unpinned ("*"), so Renovate/Flux track latest.

nodes.label: PriorityClass feather-low
nodes.rationale: Lowest tier — node-red is a best-effort tinkering workload and is the first thing evicted under node pressure.

nodes.label: ollama base-apps Kustomize overlay
nodes.rationale: The only overlay in this set with no secretGenerator and no disableNameSuffixHash — Ollama holds no credentials at all.

nodes.label: HelmRelease ollama (CPU-only inference)
nodes.rationale: gpu.enabled:false because these nodes have no GPU, which also pins the plain (non-rocm/non-cuda) image tag. CPU inference is compute-bound so cores drive tokens/sec; there is deliberately no CPU limit (a hard cap would throttle generation) — requests plus the fr-rosenau region pin keep scheduling sane. 30Gi ceph-rbd PV persists model blobs so restarts do not re-download gigabytes.

nodes.label: Model gemma4:e4b (n8n forum-application classifier)
nodes.rationale: Chosen over qwen2.5:3b because it beats it on structured extraction (correct enum/scale adherence) and is Apache 2.0 licensed for commercial use; MoE ~4B active params, 9.6Gi. CPU generation runs ~5-6 tok/s, acceptable for low-volume async classification.

nodes.label: OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1 warm-model policy
nodes.rationale: Paired with ollama.models.run so the model loads at pod start and never unloads: the cold load is brutal (~9.6Gi off Ceph-RBD = minutes) and no request should ever pay it. Callers must still pin num_ctx, because a changed context size forces a full ~30s model reload.

nodes.label: Ollama cluster-internal-only exposure (no auth)
nodes.rationale: Ollama ships no authentication whatsoever, so it gets no Ingress and no HTTPRoute — only a ClusterIP on :11434 reachable in-cluster. Exposing it publicly requires an auth proxy in front (Envoy + JWT/basic-auth/SecurityPolicy).

nodes.label: /collaboration path split to outline-collaboration (Hocuspocus)
nodes.rationale: One hostname is split across two Services at the Ingress: /collaboration goes to the Hocuspocus realtime websocket Deployment and everything else (app, API, auth, static) to outline-web — the realtime editor cannot be served by the web pods.

hyperedges.label: Harbor dual front door: one nginx-fronted ClusterIP reached by an internal Envoy HTTPRoute and an external Cloudflare tunnel Ingress, protected by PDBs
Shared cluster stateful backends every base-app plugs into: CNPG Postgres (pooled or direct), Dragonfly, Ceph RGW S3, Ceph RBD
Grafana provisioned alert pipeline: Mimir-backed rules -> flat notification policy -> Discord contact point rendered by shared templates, deduplicated by unified-alerting HA
